data.text:
‘5 YEARS OF TERROR:’ Groups stage protest at the Department of Justice in Manila, July 3, on the 5th year since the Anti-Terror Law was signed under the Duterte administration. 

Progressives assert that the Terror Law, alongside the NTF-ELCAC and the Terrorism Financing Prevention and Suppression Act, has made it easier for the government to crackdown on dissenters and activists by arbitrarily branding them as terrorists. Rights group Karapatan says at least 227 individuals have been slapped with terrorism-related charges since the Terror Law was enacted in 2020. 

Groups call for the immediate repeal of anti-democratic policies and justice for all the victims of the ‘terror laws.’

data.text:
LOOK: Rights group KARAPATAN, together with other people’s organizations, holds a protest in front of the Department of Justice (DOJ) office in Manila on Thursday, July 3, to denounce the increasing number of alleged trumped-up charges and unlawful arrests in the five years since the enactment of Republic Act No. 11479, or the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA).

The groups continue to call for the repeal of both the Anti-Terrorism Act and Republic Act No. 10168, or the Terrorism Financing Prevention and Suppression Act, which they claim are being used by the Marcos Jr. administration to criminalize activism, suppress dissent, and unjustly detain critics and human rights defenders.

📷: Mark Balmores | MB

LOOK: Residents retrieve what they can from the remains of their belongings after a fire razed their homes along Lacson Avenue in Barangay 420, Manila, on July 3, 2025. 

The blaze, which reached the third alarm, left 101 families homeless and damaged multiple residential structures. Authorities are still looking into the cause of the fire, while local officials have started distributing aid and relief to those affected. (MB photos by Mark Balmores)
